text:
Rep: Maren, thanks for jumping back on. Where did we land last time?
Maren Brannigan (HR Generalist): Oh gosh, honestly, I'd have to scroll back through my notes. So, okay, we have 430 people across ten states, the campuses are all over the place, and I'm the one who got told to replace our spreadsheet-and-prayer system. That was, what, eleven days ago when we first talked? Eleven days. And now we're finally doing the demo. I'm not complaining, I'm just thinking out loud, because it matters.
Rep: Fair. Tell me how it matters.
Maren Brannigan (HR Generalist): Well, when we talked the first time our superintendent's office was fired up. Like, do it this quarter, get me options. Then nothing for over a week, and in a week a lot happens in a school network. Our payroll clerk found one of those all-in-one tools through a friend at another district and we've kind of already started poking around in it. Set up a trial, loaded a couple of campuses. I didn't plan that! It just sort of happened while I was waiting on a calendar invite.
Rep: Understood. I can walk the full flow anyway, and I see Thaddeus is here for the integrations piece.
Thaddeus Ivarsson (IT Manager): Yeah, hi. So, single sign-on, directory sync, that's mostly what I care about. Though to be honest, I've already spent two afternoons on the other trial and the sync with our directory was fine, so, I don't know, I'm not sure what I'm hunting for here.
Rep: That's fair. Want me to show the sync anyway?
Thaddeus Ivarsson (IT Manager): Sure, sure, show it. Sorry. It's not you. It's that when this was hot I had a free week and now I've got the fall device rollout eating everything.
Maren Brannigan (HR Generalist): Yeah. Honestly, if the demo had been the week after our first call I think we'd be having a different conversation. Eleven days is a long time. The momentum, you know, it sort of drains out and then somebody else is in the room.
Rep: I hear you. I'll show it and you can decide how it compares.
Maren Brannigan (HR Generalist): Okay. Go ahead. I'll be honest, though, I'm mostly being polite at this point.

Subject: Update on our evaluation

Hi, thanks for walking us through everything. We've decided to keep going with the other tool we started setting up while we waited on the demo. Eleven days between calls was long enough that our sponsor moved on and we'd already loaded a few campuses elsewhere. Nothing against your team. Appreciate the time.

Maren

Rep: Yuki, Sunniva, good to have you both. How's your week going?
Yuki Eastwood (Chief People Officer): Busy but good. I just got back from a conference in Denver, so I'm still digging out of email. Sunniva held the fort.
Sunniva Brannigan (HR Director): I did my best. The coffee machine broke on Tuesday, so that was the real crisis.
Rep: Oh no. Any chance it's fixable?
Sunniva Brannigan (HR Director): Facilities says Friday. We'll see.
Rep: Well, thanks for making time. I wanted to close the loop on where you two are after the demo and the follow-up notes I sent.
Yuki Eastwood (Chief People Officer): Sure. First, I want to say thank you. Your team has been great, really. Everybody we dealt with was lovely, and I mean that.
Rep: That's kind of you to say.
Yuki Eastwood (Chief People Officer): So, short version, we've decided we're going a different direction. We're making a change, but it's not with you, if that makes sense.
Rep: Understood. Is there anything you'd be willing to share about how you got there? It would help us.
Yuki Eastwood (Chief People Officer): Honestly, it was a team decision, a lot of conversations. Nothing dramatic. We just landed somewhere else.
Sunniva Brannigan (HR Director): Yeah, I'd echo that. It was a good process and everyone was nice. We just went another way.
Rep: I appreciate the candor, even if it's brief. If anything changes down the road, you know where to find me.
Yuki Eastwood (Chief People Officer): Absolutely. And please tell the folks who ran the demo they were great.
Rep: I will. Anything you need from us on the way out? Records, copies of the proposal, anything like that?
Sunniva Brannigan (HR Director): No, I think we're all set. We have what we need.
Yuki Eastwood (Chief People Officer): Same. We'll keep your contact info. You never know.
Rep: Sounds good. Safe travels next time, Yuki, and I hope the coffee machine gets fixed, Sunniva.
Sunniva Brannigan (HR Director): Ha, thank you. Fingers crossed.
Yuki Eastwood (Chief People Officer): Take care. Thanks again, really.

Rep: Maren, Marisol, thank you for joining. Shall we continue with the payroll tax questions you raised?
Maren Vasquez (HR Director): Yes, please. As I mentioned, we have employees in eleven states, and that is the area where I need to be most careful. Let me give you a concrete case. We have a number of staff who live in New Jersey and work at our Pennsylvania brewery. How does your system handle the reciprocity there, and the withholding for each state?
Rep: We support reciprocity certificates, and withholding should follow the work state setup. On the specifics of the New Jersey and Pennsylvania pairing, I would want to confirm with our tax team before I commit.
Marisol Moreau (HR Director): And the local taxes? We have taproom employees in Ohio municipalities, and each city has its own income tax and its own filing schedule. Who registers us with the municipality, and who files?
Rep: I believe the filings are handled through our tax service, but I would have to check whether Ohio municipal registration is included or something you manage yourselves.
Marisol Moreau (HR Director): I see. That is the sort of answer I was hoping to avoid at this stage.
Maren Vasquez (HR Director): To be fair, the price is acceptable. I will say that plainly. If the tax handling were settled, price would not be the difficulty.
Marisol Moreau (HR Director): The other consideration, and I mention it only briefly, is that our benefits broker has recommended Tallyhold. We have worked with her for many years, and she handles our renewals, so her view carries weight with us.
Maren Vasquez (HR Director): Quite. But the larger question remains the tax filings. We cannot afford to find a gap after a quarter closes.
Rep: Understood. I will get written answers on both scenarios and send them over.
Maren Vasquez (HR Director): Thank you. Please do. We will review them, though I will be candid that we are leaning toward another direction.

Rep: Tobias, thanks for making time. You said payroll taxes were the big one.
Tobias Fonseca (COO): They are. We have staff in ten states. Dental offices spread out. Every state is a different headache.
Rep: Tell me where it hurts most.
Tobias Fonseca (COO): Illinois and Wisconsin. We have hygienists who live in one and work in the other. Reciprocity. Which state gets the withholding? Do you handle the exemption forms?
Rep: We support the forms. For the Illinois and Wisconsin setup specifically, I'd need to check how it files at the state level.
Tobias Fonseca (COO): You'd need to check. Okay. Second one. Maryland. Some counties have their own tax. Our office in one county, employee lives in another. Who sorts that out?
Rep: That I don't know offhand. We'd have to look at how the county rates are mapped.
Tobias Fonseca (COO): That's the problem. I can't hand that to my payroll person and say we'll check.
Mirela Quillfeather (IT Manager): From my side, the data export looks fine. Single sign-on works. No issue there.
Tobias Fonseca (COO): Right. Tech is fine. The taxes are not settled.
Rep: Is price a concern?
Tobias Fonseca (COO): Not really. Your number is okay. If the tax side was solid, I'd pay it. I'm not going to pay it and then get a state notice.
Rep: Fair enough. I can get you answers in writing.
Tobias Fonseca (COO): Send them. But we're probably going with Brasswick. Their people were clear on the state stuff.

Subject: Our decision

Hi, thanks for all the time. We're going with Brasswick Payroll. Your answers on state and local payroll taxes, the Illinois and Wisconsin reciprocity and the Maryland county rates, weren't firm enough for us. Pricing was fine. We need certainty there. Good luck.

Tobias

Rep: Bram, thanks for taking this. I wanted to understand where things stand.
Bram Ibarra (Head of HR): Yeah. Honestly, I'm tired, so I'll just be straight with you. It was thirteen days. Thirteen days from the first call to the demo. When I called you, I had a green light from my director and a really bad month of payroll fixes behind me. I wanted something fast.
Rep: I'm sorry about the gap. It's on us.
Bram Ibarra (Head of HR): I know. And look, I understand calendars. But my director's patience is not a renewable resource. By day six she was asking me why we didn't have anything lined up. By day ten she'd gone to a vendor our benefits team already had a relationship with.
Tobias Vasquez (Benefits Manager): That's me, kind of. I'd been using their open enrollment tool for two years, so when Bram's director asked, it was an easy yes.
Bram Ibarra (Head of HR): So we kicked off a project with them. It's not finished, but it's started, and once people have started something, they don't want to restart it.
Tobias Vasquez (Benefits Manager): And the Operations side is already sold. Our operations director is sick of meetings.
Bram Ibarra (Head of HR): Yeah. By the time you showed up for the demo, we were already in a second set of meetings with somebody else. I almost canceled.
Rep: I appreciate you being honest. Is there anything at all you'd change about how we handled it?
Bram Ibarra (Head of HR): Show up sooner. That's it. Thirteen days is a lifetime when somebody's boss is asking questions.
Rep: Understood.
Bram Ibarra (Head of HR): I'll keep your info. It's just, the moment passed.

Rep: Hollis, Teodoro, thanks for joining. Let's talk about where we are.
Hollis Moreau (Office Manager): Okay. I'll be short. We called you twelve days before the demo. Twelve. That's too long.
Rep: I hear that. I'm sorry.
Hollis Moreau (Office Manager): I'm not mad. It's just fact. We were hot on this. Payroll was a mess. We staff temps, so every week is a new batch.
Teodoro Delacroix (Finance Director): I'll add. When we first talked, I was asked to find something by end of month. Then days pass. Nothing. I told Hollis, we can't wait.
Hollis Moreau (Office Manager): So we asked our broker for another option. He pointed us to Corvane. They had a demo in two days.
Rep: And you've moved forward with them?
Hollis Moreau (Office Manager): We started. Setup call is done. Data is partly loaded.
Teodoro Delacroix (Finance Director): It's not signed in blood. But we're in it. I'm not restarting.
Rep: I understand. Is there anything about the product you'd want us to know?
Hollis Moreau (Office Manager): No. We didn't even get to that. You know what? The demo you gave today looked good. But it came late.
Teodoro Delacroix (Finance Director): Right. Good demo. Wrong week. Twelve days ago it would have been different.
Hollis Moreau (Office Manager): I told my COO the same thing. He asked who was slow. I said the calendar.
Rep: Fair. I'll take that as feedback for our team.
Hollis Moreau (Office Manager): Please do. We liked your rep. We liked the tool. We just couldn't sit still.
Teodoro Delacroix (Finance Director): Same here. It's timing. That's all I've got.
Rep: Thanks for telling me straight.

Rep: Kofi, Priya, thanks for coming back. You had questions on tax.
Kofi Lindgren (Chief People Officer): We do. We've got people in eight states. Priya's the one who has to sign off on compliance.
Priya Fonseca (Compliance Lead): Right. Let me ask this. We have drivers who live in Virginia, work out of D.C., and some in Maryland. Reciprocity. Which state gets the withholding? What does your system do?
Rep: We'd handle the withholding by work location, with reciprocity forms on file. For that specific Virginia and D.C. arrangement, I'd have to check with our tax group.
Priya Fonseca (Compliance Lead): Okay. Another one. Kentucky. Local occupational taxes. Counties and cities. We have a warehouse there. Who registers us? Who files?
Rep: I'm not certain. We'd have to check on the local registrations.
Priya Fonseca (Compliance Lead): That's a pattern. 'We'd have to check.'
Kofi Lindgren (Chief People Officer): Price is fine. I'll say it once. Your number is fair. If this was nailed down, I'd sign.
Priya Fonseca (Compliance Lead): I can't sign off on a maybe. State notices come to me.
Kofi Lindgren (Chief People Officer): There's another thing. Our budget got frozen last month. Finance said no new systems this half. That's a pause, not a no.
Rep: Understood. If I get you written answers on both cases, would that help?
Priya Fonseca (Compliance Lead): It would. But I'd want to see actual filings. Not a promise.
Kofi Lindgren (Chief People Officer): We'll look at them. But I'm not going to promise a timeline.
Rep: Fair enough. I'll send them this week.
Kofi Lindgren (Chief People Officer): Good. Thanks.

Rep: Rafferty, thanks. Yuki's here too?
Rafferty Yarrow (COO): Yeah. She's listening. I'll be honest, I'm tired. Long week. Let me just ask what I need.
Rep: Go ahead.
Rafferty Yarrow (COO): Eight states. A developer moves from Texas to Colorado in July. Mid-year. What happens to withholding? Local taxes? Denver has that head tax thing.
Rep: We'd update the work state and start Colorado withholding. For Denver's occupational privilege tax specifically, I'd have to check how we register that.
Rafferty Yarrow (COO): Okay. And if we hire someone remote in a state we've never been in? Who registers us with the state?
Rep: I'm not sure on the exact process there. We'd have to look.
Yuki Rourke (General Manager): That's two for two.
Rafferty Yarrow (COO): Price is fine, by the way. It's not the issue. If you could tell me this stuff cleanly, I'd pay it.
Rep: I can get answers in writing.
Rafferty Yarrow (COO): Do that. But we're tired of waiting on maybes.

Rep: Bram, thanks for making time today. Rafferty, welcome.
Bram Underhill (Office Manager): Thanks. I'll start with the numbers, because I keep a log. First call with you was on the third. Demo was on the nineteenth. That's sixteen days. I counted twice.
Rep: I'm sorry. That's longer than it should have been.
Bram Underhill (Office Manager): It is what it is. But here's what it cost us. On the third, we had a sponsor, our owner, who wanted this wrapped by the end of the month. By the tenth, he'd asked me three times what the status was. By the twelfth, I had a proposal in hand from Brasswick, because their rep called back in a day and a half.
Rafferty Lindgren (Head of People): And I'll add the part from my side. Once we had Brasswick's implementation timeline on the table, it became a question of, do we pause that to see Lanternmere, or do we keep going? We kept going.
Bram Underhill (Office Manager): We've signed a letter of intent. Not final, but close, roughly eighty percent done. I'd say we're about two weeks from kickoff.
Rep: Understood. Is there anything in the demo itself that missed?
Bram Underhill (Office Manager): No, nothing. It looked fine. The timing is the whole story. Sixteen days. If you'd been here in four, we'd likely have this conversation differently.
Rafferty Lindgren (Head of People): Probably true. It's a shame, really.
Rep: Thanks for being specific. I'll pass it on.

Subject: Following up

Hi, thank you for the demo. We've decided to proceed with Brasswick. The sixteen days between our first call and the demo meant our owner had lost patience and we'd already started elsewhere. Nothing about your product. Just timing.

Bram

Rep: Noor, thanks for rejoining. Hollis, good to meet you.
Noor Hollander (Director of Operations): Yeah. Hi. I'm tired, so apologies if I ramble. We're a design studio, six states, mostly remote now. That's what keeps me up.
Rep: Tell me about it.
Noor Hollander (Director of Operations): Okay. We have a designer in Portland. Oregon has that metro tax and the transit tax on top of the state one. Who registers us for those? Who files the quarterly forms?
Rep: We handle state withholding. For the Portland metro and transit taxes, I'd have to check with our tax team about whether that's included.
Noor Hollander (Director of Operations): Okay. And a second one. We've got someone in Washington state who's moving to Oregon in August. Mid-year. She's paid by us the whole time. What happens to her withholding? Her paid family leave? Her unemployment?
Rep: That's a good one. I don't want to guess. We'd have to check how the state change gets processed mid-year.
Hollis Oyelaran (Head of People): We hear 'we'd have to check' a lot, Noor.
Noor Hollander (Director of Operations): We do. Look, to be fair, price is fine. Your number was in range. I'm not going to pretend it's a money thing.
Hollis Oyelaran (Head of People): Right. If the tax handling was clear, we'd be signing today.
Noor Hollander (Director of Operations): The thing is, when we get one of those wrong, it's me on the phone with a state agency. And I'm too tired for that.
Rep: Understood. I can send written answers on both.
Noor Hollander (Director of Operations): Please. But I'll be straight, we're also talking to Brasswick, and they answered the Oregon question on the spot.
Rep: Noted. Thank you for the honesty.

Rep: Marisol, thanks for jumping on. Ingrid, you too.
Marisol Yarrow (Office Manager): Yep, hi. Let's make this quick, I know everyone's busy. I'll tell you where we're at. We're going with Tallyhold.
Rep: Okay. I appreciate you telling me directly.
Marisol Yarrow (Office Manager): It's not about you. Our broker put the bundle in front of us. Payroll, benefits, the whole thing under one roof. She's the one who handles our renewals every year, and I trust her. When she says this is the package, I listen.
Rep: Did you get a chance to compare anything side by side?
Marisol Yarrow (Office Manager): Not really. I looked at yours, and it looked fine. But our broker already had the pricing worked out for the bundle, and she'd already talked to the carriers.
Ingrid Thorsen (Payroll Manager): From my side, I'd like to say I'd have liked to see more. I do payroll. I'd have liked to test your tax setup. We have people in seven states, and that's something I worry about.
Marisol Yarrow (Office Manager): Right, seven states. But that's not a deal-breaker. It's a thing we'll sort out with whoever we use.
Ingrid Thorsen (Payroll Manager): Mm. I'd still have liked to see it.
Marisol Yarrow (Office Manager): But I made the call. Our broker says go, I go. It saves me a lot of work during renewals.
Rep: I understand. If anything changes, I'm here.
Marisol Yarrow (Office Manager): Thanks. And thanks for the demo. It was a good one.

Rep: Teodoro, Wren, thanks for hopping on. How's everything over at Nettlebed?
Teodoro Zeller (HR Generalist): Oh, you know, it's freight. Trucks do what trucks do. Somebody's always got a flat or a, what do you call it, a delay. Wren was just telling me about her kid's soccer thing this weekend, so we've been catching up.
Wren Zeller (COO): Ha, yes. Third place, which, honestly, they were thrilled about. We got ice cream.
Rep: That's great. Well, I wanted to follow up on the demo and see where you two are at.
Teodoro Zeller (HR Generalist): Right, right. So, I wanted to say first, thank you. Everyone was so nice. And, um, we talked it over, Wren and I and a couple of the others, and we've decided to go a different direction.
Rep: Okay. I appreciate you telling me.
Wren Zeller (COO): We're making a change, but it's not with you. I hope that's clear. We just wanted to let you know before you heard it elsewhere.
Rep: I appreciate that. Is there anything you'd feel comfortable sharing?
Teodoro Zeller (HR Generalist): Oh, I wish I had a big story for you. It's really just, we had a lot of conversations and this is where we ended up. Everyone was happy with how it went.
Wren Zeller (COO): Yes, no complaints about the process at all. Just a different direction.
Rep: Sure. Well, if anything changes, I'd be glad to pick it back up.
Teodoro Zeller (HR Generalist): Absolutely. We'll keep your card. And tell your team thanks again.
Wren Zeller (COO): Yes. And good luck with the rest of your quarter.
Rep: Thanks, you too. Take care, both of you.

Rep: Casper, Marisol, thanks for joining. I wanted to hear where you stand.
Casper Brannigan (People Operations Lead): Sure. Short answer, we're going with Tallyhold. I wanted to tell you personally.
Rep: I appreciate that. Can you share what tipped it?
Casper Brannigan (People Operations Lead): Our broker. She put the bundle in front of us, payroll, benefits, and the administration all together. She's handled our renewals for years. I trust her, and when she says this is the one, that carries weight.
Marisol Vasquez (CFO): From the finance side, I'll be direct. We didn't do a deep side-by-side. Our broker brought us the package and it was priced cleanly. She also manages the renewal, so it's one conversation instead of three.
Rep: Understood. Did anything in our demo concern you?
Casper Brannigan (People Operations Lead): No. The demo was fine. Your rep was sharp. It's honestly not about the product.
Marisol Vasquez (CFO): Agreed. It's the relationship. We've worked with her a long time.
Rep: Fair. If the situation changes at renewal time, I'm happy to talk.
Casper Brannigan (People Operations Lead): We'll keep that in mind. Thanks for your time.
Marisol Vasquez (CFO): Yes, thank you. It was a good process.

Rep: Teodoro, thanks for coming back. You have people in ten states?
Teodoro Tillbrook (COO): Ten. Yeah. Printing plants, packaging, a couple of sales folks working from home. I'm tired, so let me skip the small talk. State taxes. That's what I need to be sure about.
Rep: Go ahead.
Teodoro Tillbrook (COO): We have a pressman who lives in Indiana and works at our plant in Kentucky. Reciprocity doesn't cover that, as I understand it. Who sets up the right withholding? Who files in both?
Rep: We'd handle withholding by work state, and I believe the resident state is configured separately. For that exact pair, I'd have to check with our tax people.
Teodoro Tillbrook (COO): Okay. Second one. We hire a sales rep who works from her kitchen in a state we've never done business in. Registration, unemployment account, all of it. Who does that?
Rep: I'm honestly not sure how much of the registration we do for you. We'd have to check.
Emeka Moreau (HR Director): That's what worries me. We can't live on 'check'.
Teodoro Tillbrook (COO): Price is okay, I want to say that. I'm not here to haggle. If the tax part was firm, I'd pay it.
Emeka Moreau (HR Director): And one more small thing. We recruit constantly, and your system doesn't have an applicant tracking module. We'd be bolting something on. That's annoying, but it's a side issue.
Teodoro Tillbrook (COO): Yeah, minor. The taxes are what matters.
Rep: Understood. I'll send you written answers.
Teodoro Tillbrook (COO): Send them. We're also looking at Corvane, and so far they've been clearer on the state side.

Rep: Bastian, Amara, thanks for joining. You wanted to go deeper on payroll taxes?
Bastian Moreau (Chief People Officer): Yes, so, okay, we're only in five states, which sounds simple, but I keep thinking about it. Five states, and probably three of those are different in some weird way. So let me think out loud. We have an engineer who lives in Pennsylvania but, um, her office is in Ohio, and Pennsylvania has that local services tax, which, wait, is that what it's called? The one that's like fifty-two dollars a year?
Rep: Yes, the local services tax. And Ohio municipalities have their own. For how we calculate and file both together, I'd need to confirm with our tax team.
Bastian Moreau (Chief People Officer): So that's a no-answer. Okay. Let me try another. Michigan. We've got a guy in Detroit. Detroit city income tax, resident versus non-resident rates. Do you do that?
Rep: I believe we support city taxes in Michigan, but I'd have to check Detroit specifically.
Amara Vasquez (Operations Director): That's what we heard last time too, Bastian.
Bastian Moreau (Chief People Officer): Right. And I'll say, the price isn't my worry. It's fair. If I trusted the tax stuff, we'd do it.
Amara Vasquez (Operations Director): We can't have somebody's city return wrong because the system didn't know about it.
Bastian Moreau (Chief People Officer): Exactly. It's one of those things where it's only five states but each one has a quirk.
Rep: I understand. I'll get you a written answer on both.
Bastian Moreau (Chief People Officer): Appreciate it. But I'm leaning toward the Tallyhold folks since they said yes to both.

Subject: Thanks, and our decision

Hi, thanks for working with us. We're going with Tallyhold. They could confirm Pennsylvania local services tax and Detroit city income tax filing right away, and we couldn't get that certainty from your side. Price was fine. Hope we cross paths again.

Bastian

Rep: Odalys, hi, and Ravi. Thanks for coming back to me.
Odalys Ashgrove (HR Director): Of course. Oh, I love your background, is that a lake? Never mind. Okay. So, we have vet clinics in six states. And my big hang-up, you know what it is, it's payroll tax. I just can't get comfortable.
Rep: Tell me what you're seeing.
Odalys Ashgrove (HR Director): So, we have a vet tech who lives in North Dakota and works at a clinic in Minnesota, or the other way around, I always mix it up. There's a reciprocity agreement, I know that, and she gave us a form. But does your system just know to stop the Minnesota withholding? Or do we have to babysit it?
Rep: We support the exemption on file. For that Minnesota and North Dakota case, I'd have to check how it sets the state.
Odalys Ashgrove (HR Director): Right, right. And then Indiana, where each county has its own rate, and one of our clinics straddles a county line. Who maps that?
Rep: I'm not sure. We'd have to check on the county tables.
Ravi Ibarra (Head of People): It's the checking that bothers us, honestly.
Odalys Ashgrove (HR Director): Yes. And price, it's fine, I'm not here to complain about price. We'd pay it. But I need the tax part to be solid.
Rep: Understood. I'll send written answers.
Odalys Ashgrove (HR Director): Please. But we're likely going with Tallyhold, to be honest.

Rep: Bram, thanks for the time. Idris, glad you're on.
Bram Oyelaran (People Operations Lead): Hi. I'll be direct. We're going with Tallyhold.
Rep: Thanks for telling me. What led there?
Bram Oyelaran (People Operations Lead): Our broker. She brought us the bundle. Payroll, benefits, all in one. She handles our renewals. We've worked with her for years. I trust her.
Idris Abernethy (Head of People): I'll add. We didn't dig into side-by-sides. Our broker put one package in front of us. The numbers worked. The carriers are lined up.
Bram Oyelaran (People Operations Lead): It's less work for us. One contact at renewal. That matters.
Rep: Understood. Anything from the demo that gave you pause?
Bram Oyelaran (People Operations Lead): No. Demo was clean. Your rep knew the product. That's not why.
Idris Abernethy (Head of Payroll Manager): Same from payroll. Nothing wrong with yours.
Rep: Fair. If your broker's package changes next year, I'd welcome a call.
Bram Oyelaran (People Operations Lead): Noted. Thanks for being understanding.
Idris Abernethy (Head of People): Yes. Thanks for the time.

Rep: Mirela, Delphine, thanks for joining. You wanted to go through taxes again.
Mirela Ivarsson (Director of Operations): Yeah. I'm tired, so forgive me. Twelve states. Logistics. People move around. That's the whole problem.
Rep: Walk me through a case.
Mirela Ivarsson (Director of Operations): Okay. Registrations. We just hired a dispatcher in Washington state. Washington has the paid family leave premiums and the long-term care thing. We've never had an employee there. Who registers us with the state? Who sets up the accounts?
Rep: We'd handle the withholding setup. For Washington's paid family leave and the care program, I'd have to check what we do versus what you register on your own.
Mirela Ivarsson (Director of Operations): Okay. Second. California. A driver based in Fresno. State disability insurance, and the city tax rules for the drivers who pass through. Do you track which days they work where?
Rep: I'm not sure we track that. We'd have to check.
Delphine Whitlock (COO): That's the part I need to hear, Mirela. It's the same answer as last week.
Mirela Ivarsson (Director of Operations): Yeah. The price I'll tell you, it's fine. Not the issue. If the tax side was solid, we'd move.
Delphine Whitlock (COO): We can't have a filing miss in twelve states. It's one thing in two. In twelve it's a full-time job.
Mirela Ivarsson (Director of Operations): Corvane gave us a list of what they file for each state. In writing. That's what we need.
Rep: Understood. I'll try to get you the same.
Mirela Ivarsson (Director of Operations): Please try. But I'll tell you straight, we're probably done.

Subject: Our decision

Hi, thank you for the time and the patience. We've decided to go with Corvane. They gave us a written list of what they register and file in each of our twelve states, including Washington and California, and we couldn't get that from you. Price was not the issue. Best of luck.

Mirela

Rep: Annelise, Jules, thank you for joining. I would like to understand where you stand.
Annelise Hollander (Operations Manager): Certainly. I will be candid. We are not proceeding with Lanternmere.
Rep: I appreciate your directness. May I ask what led to that?
Annelise Hollander (Operations Manager): It is, I think, a matter of timing. We spoke to you on a Monday. The demonstration did not occur until the following Sunday evening, or rather it was scheduled for the Monday after that, six days later. I recognize that this may not sound long.
